decisions.reason: The product showed continued dedicated promotion, a clear upgrade path from BASIC 518 to 518 FLEX, and signs of customer acceptance, so its upside appears proven enough to justify staying in the portfolio.
The AK flail shredder line was still being actively updated for Stage V emissions in 2019, indicating regulatory adaptation and low incremental cost to keep this established mobile option open.
Its move from a website mention to a dedicated product page suggests rising commitment and still-open growth potential in a core mobile processing segment.

After only being mentioned in 2018 and disappearing from the website in 2019, the available evidence suggests the market test revealed weak prospects relative to the cost of maintaining a specialized stationary product.

The CERON stationary pre-shredder family remained prominently presented and was described as setting standards in its segment, which points to strong strategic fit and encouraging early market validation.
